dx_raw:
DIAGNOSIS: Functional neurological symptom disorder (functional gait disorder with astasia-abasia) — manifested as recurrent, incongruent, slow controlled falls to the floor with a positive Hoover sign but fully preserved motor, sensory and reflex examination, normal neuroimaging and normal blood work.

1. Frontal lobe (gait apraxia) or normal-pressure hydrocephalus — less likely given normal CT head, preserved cognition, positive Hoover sign, and dramatic normalisation with distraction
2. Paroxysmal non-kinesigenic movement disorder / episodic ataxia — possible but unlikely given sustained and reproducible nature of the falls and normal coordination
3. Rare organic mimic such as a basal ganglia or brainstem lesion (e.g., atypical parkinsonian fall syndrome) — would not normally produce a positive Hoover sign or normal CT, and neurological exam is otherwise intact
